title: The Storm Changes the Grammar: Why God Stops Calling the Sailors 'You'

attack_summary.1_substrate: VERIFIED from corpus morphology. 10:22 addressee opens 2MP (yusayyiru-KUM, kun-TUM) -> turns to 3rd person (jarayna 3FP + bi-HIM 3MP, farihu 3MP, ja'a-HUM 3MP, zannu 3MP, uhita bi-HIM 3MP, da'aw 3MP) -> quoted vow anjay-TA-na = 2MS aimed at GOD + 1P 'us'. Every person value the reveal leans on is a fixed morphological feature. No wrong fact in the single-verse substrate.
attack_summary.2_imposed_test: The load-bearing single-verse claim is REAL and RECOVERED, not imposed. al-Jalalayn on wa-jarayna bihim states VERBATIM 'fihi iltifat 'an al-khitab' (pulled directly via cross_reference_tafsir). The classical tradition named this exact turn on this exact word. Passes the imposed test on the core. The IMPOSED risk lives only in two secondary layers (see broken_claims): the cross-passage 'repeats' claim and the psychological meaning assigned to the device.
attack_summary.3_disguised_count: PASS. Reveal is about grammatical PERSON shifts (khitab->ghayba->address-to-God) within one verse, not word frequency. Not a count in disguise.
attack_summary.4_overlap: PASS. content/tadabbur/010-yunus/ayahs-021-024.md covers the passage psychologically (7-item linguistic journey: adhaqna/tasted-mercy, makr, 'storms strip soul to tawhid', rescue-without-reform, baghy-boomerang, zukhruf, hasidan) but NEVER spotlights the pronoun/person choreography or names the iltifat. Proposal already says cross-link, don't restate. No published article in published-articles.md covers 10:22 or an iltifat/khitab->ghayba pronoun-shift piece (existing 'grammar' articles are on other verses: verb-fork, grammar-of-permission, grammar-of-tyranny, two-processions). Thematic proximity to section 3 ('storms strip to tawhid') is real but the pronoun MECHANISM is genuinely fresh.
attack_summary.5_quran_only: PASS. Payoff rests on al-Jalalayn (tafsir) + corpus morphology + Quranic parallels. No hadith dependency.
attack_summary.6_hostile_tweet: 'Every mufassir knows 10:22 has an iltifat, al-Jalalayn says so in six words. You dressed a stock grammar note as a theology of distance-written-into-pronouns, then claimed it *repeats* across three verses where it doesn't: 17:67 never leaves you, 31:32 never uses you.' -> The single-verse core survives (al-Jalalayn is real and verbatim). The cross-passage 'repeats' claim does NOT survive and must be reframed.

broken_claims: ILTIFAT-1 reveal asserts 'The choreography repeats across the sea-rescues (6:63-64, 17:67, 31:32)'. It does NOT repeat: 17:67 is uniform 2MP throughout (massa-KUM / najja-KUM / a'rad-TUM) with NO turn to ghayba; 31:32 is uniform 3MP throughout (ghashiya-HUM / da'aw / najja-HUM) with NO khitab at all; 6:63's rescue-vow is anja-NA = 3MS verb ('if HE saves us'), NOT the 2MS 'if YOU save us' of 10:22. Only 10:22 completes the full you->them->You-to-God arc. Claiming the pattern 'repeats' imposes a uniformity the corpus refutes.

Thesis asserts 'al-Zamakhshari uses 10:22 in al-Kashshaf as the paradigm case of the turn from address to absence' and exhibit adds 'al-Razi discusses it'. UNVERIFIABLE with available tools (cross_reference_tafsir pulls only Ibn Kathir/Tabari/Muyassar/Jalalayn, not Kashshaf/Razi). 'The paradigm case' is also an overstatement: the canonical textbook paradigm of iltifat in the balaghah tradition is al-Fatiha's iyyaka na'budu, not 10:22. This claim is NOT load-bearing (al-Jalalayn's verbatim note fully carries the grounding), so it does not refute the proposal, but it must be sourced or softened.

The psychological MEANING assigned to the device ('distance from God is written into the pronouns before it is felt in the heart', 'comfort makes them forget Him') is the candidate's modern reflection. al-Jalalayn names the DEVICE but gives no reason; Zamakhshari's classical nukta for this iltifat is typically ta'ajjub (casting them as an absent party whose ingratitude is marveled at) - adjacent but not identical. Presenting the comfort->forgetting reading as the mufassir's stated interpretation would overclaim.
required_corrections: (1) Reframe the cross-passage layer: do NOT say the choreography 'repeats'. State plainly that these sea-rescue verses form a FAMILY that handles the God-address differently - 17:67 stays entirely in 2nd person, 31:32 stays entirely in 3rd, 6:63's vow says 'He' (anja-NA, 3MS) - and that ONLY 10:22 completes the full you->them->You-to-God turn. Keep this whole map bracketed as modern synthesis (candidate already does). (2) Verify the al-Zamakhshari/al-Razi citations from primary sources before asserting them; drop the 'paradigm case' superlative unless independently sourced - assert the classical grounding on the al-Jalalayn verbatim note, which is confirmed. (3) Attribute the DEVICE (iltifat at wa-jarayna bihim) to classical tafsir, but present the psychological reading (comfort->forgetting->distance) explicitly as tadabbur/reflection, not as the mufassir's stated reason. (4) Keep the narrative voice honest: the storyline stays in 3rd person through the ENTIRE storm (ja'ahum/zannu/da'aw all 3MP); the only 2nd person that returns is the sailors' own quoted speech TO God (anjayta-na) - the narration never resumes addressing them as 'you' (ground_notes already flags this - reinforce). (5) Distinguish the two different second persons: the opening 'you' (2MP) is God->mankind; the storm 'You' (2MS) is mankind->God. Do not blur them into a single 'you' thread - the direction of address reverses, which is the actual theological point.
notes: Load-bearing claim is solid and among the strongest in the pool: 10:22 carries a classically-NAMED iltifat (khitab->ghayba) at wa-jarayna bihim, verified both from corpus person-features and verbatim in al-Jalalayn ('fihi iltifat 'an al-khitab', pulled live). Not a disguised count, Quran-only, no fatal overlap (existing 010-yunus/ayahs-021-024.md covers the psychology, not the grammar; no published article covers it). The three defects are all in secondary/decorative layers the candidate already marks as modern - they trim overreach rather than break the thesis. SURVIVES with required corrections.
